value.barrier_note: ONS: 41% of UK businesses with 10 or more employees report no barriers to adoption. Among those that do, a lack of expertise is one of the most cited, around 18% among businesses with 100 to 249 employees; cost affects around 7% to 14% across size bands; regulatory issues are less frequently reported.
facts: 55% of employees use AI for work or education (Great Britain, May to June 2026), against 34.9% of businesses with 10+ employees (June 2026): employees are ahead of their employers.
Free-to-use software and the purchase of external, ready-to-use software are the most common ways UK businesses adopt AI.
Improving business operations is the most common use, reported by 56% to 66% of AI-using businesses across size bands.

b2b.source: ONS Business Insights and Conditions Survey, AI in UK businesses (June 2026); DBT Business Population Estimates 2025 (counts)
b2b.note: Not comparable one-for-one with Eurostat. 'genai' = businesses with 10+ employees using large language models (18%, the most widely used AI type). Large = 49% of businesses with 250+ employees used at least one AI technology. Counts: UK private sector businesses and employment by size (DBT). Size-level generative-AI use and barriers are not published; the 10+ figure is applied to every size class. Facts and barriers from the ONS article 'Artificial intelligence in UK businesses: 2023 to 2026' (20 July 2026).

facts: Among the largest ChatGPT Enterprise markets outside the US by number of customers.
